subject.title: fix: harden security and release integrity

question: Should ClickClack preserve trusted private callback destinations through explicit configuration, or intentionally make public-only callback egress a breaking permanent contract?
rationale: The secure default is clear, but deciding whether existing self-hosted private callbacks remain supported is a security-versus-compatibility policy choice that tests and CI cannot resolve.

options.title: Secure default with allowlist
options.body: Keep public-only egress by default and add a narrow explicit hostname or CIDR allowlist with upgrade documentation and focused tests.

options.title: Public-only breaking contract
options.body: Reject all private callback destinations permanently and provide explicit migration documentation and upgrade proof for affected installations.

options.title: Split callback hardening
options.body: Pause the callback portion and land the independent storage, client, contract, and release changes in narrower reviewed PRs.

recommendation.title: Secure default with allowlist
recommendation.body: Keep public-only egress by default and add a narrow explicit hostname or CIDR allowlist with upgrade documentation and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned repository member owns the current callback-security implementation and the related release follow-up context.
